correctness.rationale: Ore products are expanded coefficientwise in a quadratic basis 1,theta. Their three independent commutator coordinates are exactly the wedge minors of (V,B,D) over S=F_s[z]/z^a; no characteristic restriction is hidden. Kernel of that pairing against all vectors is zero, giving the center. For a vector of valuation t, a GL_3(S) change of coordinates reduces the centralizer to the annihilator of z^t in two coordinates. This proves all centralizer sizes and counts; geometric summation gives the stated probability. The independent brute checker (supplied as a file) enumerated every pair in ring sizes 64,1024,729 and direct centralizers of 12 elements in F16; all passed. The general claim depends on algebraic proof, not exhaustive computation outside these cases.

originality.rationale: A specific all-parameter centralizer-order law for odd truncated quadratic Galois-skew Ore local rings was not implied by the closely inspected finite-ring probability spectra, finite-field skew-polynomial isomorphism classification, finite skew-code results, or the differently-hypothesized general Ore-centralizer work. The new mathematical step is an exact exterior-minor model over a variable-length finite chain ring; existing general formulas for commuting probability still require this special ring-specific calculation. The unindexed literature remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: This class is a natural family of finite local noncommutative Ore quotients with unbounded Loewy length. Element-centralizer order spectra and commuting probability are intrinsic and broadly used ring invariants. The exact three-minor geometric model provides a structural bridge to modules over chain rings and determines every centralizer-size stratum for all residue field sizes and all odd truncations, including characteristic two, plus the precise exponential decay constant. Neither a single numerical example nor a mere specialization of the known centralizer averaging identity would provide this value.
